description:
Full ticket-policy epic fixture: the published-cutover proof. Scope policy is a **sibling** fixture issue, not a branch inside this script.

## Background

Prove the user-visible loop: ready ticket → orchestrate implementation → settle (prose OK) → parent does not close → independent review → parent fix|file|reject → close → dependent unlocks from bw ready → epic close exits goal mode and forgets the group.

Script the parent (deterministic fake completions). No paid LLM.

## Scenario (ticket policy only)

1. Epic with two parallel tickets and one dependent.
2. `/bw run` inject, one open group.
3. Two implementation children on shared branch.
4. **Required:** overlap notice + one peer message (C is a blocker).
5. **Required:** one live child → parent question (`parentMessage`) then continue; mail vs settle does not double-complete.
6. Settlement does not close.
7. Review child on one clean ticket and one with findings; scripted parent dispositions fix, file, reject.
8. Fix assignment + re-review.
9. Dependent unlocks only after parent closed the blocker ticket (`bw ready`), not because a child settled.
10. Epic close exits run and forgets group.
11. No tmux/landing/registry/worker tools.

## Success criteria

- tmux binary not required.
- Packet coalescing asserted if two completions are arranged near-simultaneously.
- Quality commands run as implementer/reviewer actions in the fixture, not a beadwork runner.

## Test plan / logging

Structured logs per step: timestamp, step, policy=ticket, issue ids, child ids, group id, event class, packet seq, bw status.

On failure: last packets, `bw ready`, `bw show` epic, minion list, whether tmux appeared in PATH probes.

## Considerations

Share the scripted-parent harness with the scope-policy fixture. Do not mix policies in one test.

comments.text: Published-cutover proof. Script parent turns. Separate ticket-policy fixture; do not mix scope policy into the same ambiguous test.

title: Prove one epic end-to-end with ticket review and no tmux
